callpeak.label: Call narrow peaks
callpeak.description: Call narrow peaks in public chromosome 22 ChIP-seq reads against the corresponding control. The example uses a fixed 150 bp extension and q-value cutoff 0.05.

callpeak-broad.label: Call broad peaks
callpeak-broad.description: Call broad enrichment regions on the same public ChIP-seq subset. Adjust genome size, model and thresholds for your own experiment.

callpeak-paired.label: Call peaks from paired fragments
callpeak-paired.description: Use observed fragment intervals in MACS3 three-column BEDPE format. This format differs from the six-column BEDTools BEDPE format.

filterdup.label: Filter duplicate alignments
filterdup.description: Keep one read at each genomic position and strand in the public ChIP-seq example.

pileup.label: Generate a coverage track
pileup.description: Extend ChIP-seq reads to 150 bp and write their coverage as a bedGraph track. This output can be used by later commands.

randsample.label: Sample reads reproducibly
randsample.description: Keep approximately 10% of the public ChIP-seq reads using random seed 42.

predictd.label: Measure paired fragment lengths
predictd.description: Report the mean fragment length from the public paired-end alignment subset. In paired-end mode this command reports to the command log and does not create a model file.

bdgpeakcall.label: Call peaks from a score track
bdgpeakcall.description: Call regions with scores at least 5, length at least 50 bp and gaps no larger than 50 bp in a small synthetic track with known regions.

bdgbroadcall.label: Call broad regions from a score track
bdgbroadcall.description: Call nested broad regions in a synthetic score track with peak cutoff 5 and linking cutoff 2.

bdgcmp.label: Compare treatment and control tracks
bdgcmp.description: Calculate Poisson enrichment scores from synthetic treatment and background tracks.

bdgopt.label: Transform track scores
bdgopt.description: Multiply every score in the synthetic bedGraph track by 2.

cmbreps.label: Combine replicate score tracks
cmbreps.description: Average scores from two synthetic tracks with matching genomic coordinates.

bdgdiff.label: Find differential regions
bdgdiff.description: Compare synthetic treatment and background tracks for two conditions using log-likelihood ratio cutoff 1.

refinepeak.label: Refine candidate peak summits
refinepeak.description: Refine candidate summits using the public single-end ChIP-seq reads.

hmmratac.label: Analyze ATAC cutoffs
hmmratac.description: Run HMMRATAC cutoff analysis on a public yeast chromosome I ATAC-seq subset. The report helps choose training and decoding cutoffs; this preset stops before model training.

callvar.label: Call variants in peak regions
callvar.description: Call variants in public indexed treatment and control BAM files over supplied peak regions. Browser execution uses one process.

help.label: Show command-line help
help.description: Show all MACS3 subcommands. Edit the arguments to ["callpeak", "--help"] or another subcommand for its full options.

version.label: Show MACS3 version
version.description: Print the bundled upstream MACS3 version. No data is needed.

hmmratac-model.label: Train and apply a Poisson ATAC model
hmmratac-model.description: Train a Poisson HMM on selected regions of the public yeast chromosome I ATAC-seq subset, then decode accessible regions with 1 kb flanks. Fixed fragment distributions and a recorded random seed make this small example reproducible.

hmmratac-gaussian.label: Train and apply a Gaussian ATAC model
hmmratac-gaussian.description: Learn the fragment distributions and select training regions using upstream defaults, then train and apply a Gaussian HMM to the public yeast chromosome I subset. A recorded random seed and 1 kb flanks support reproducible comparisons.

macs3.label: Public MACS3 examples and synthetic score tracks
macs3.description: Public upstream ChIP-seq, paired-end, ATAC-seq and variant fixtures, plus clearly labeled synthetic score tracks for inspecting exact transformations. These small subsets demonstrate commands; they do not describe the full experiments.
